keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Hospice volunteering varies significantly by location — knowing the city or region determines which specific organizations and programs are actually searchable and reachable.

Hospice volunteering covers a wide range of roles (direct patient companionship, administrative support, bereavement support, errands, etc.) — knowing which types the user is open to shapes what to look for.
Whether this is for the user personally, a group, a student requirement, or someone else changes the eligibility criteria and the type of opportunities that are relevant.
Available time per week or month is a hard limit — many hospice programs require a minimum commitment, so knowing this filters out incompatible opportunities immediately.
Some people want in-home patient visits; others prefer facility-based or non-clinical roles. Emotional comfort level and personal preferences drastically change which roles to prioritise.
Understanding what 'research' means here — whether the user wants a simple list of contacts, a comparison table, or a ready-to-apply shortlist — determines the format and depth of the output.

The user may consider this task done when they have a list of organisations, when they've made first contact, or when they've actually registered — knowing the finish line shapes how far the plan needs to go.
